_doc: The failure-class index (#4122, chairman 2026-10-08). A CLASS is a way the org fails that has happened more than once; the question asked of every defect before it closes is 'where else can this occur, and what stops it everywhere?'. THIS FILE HOLDS DEFINITIONS ONLY: id, name, guard. An INSTANCE is a closed row carrying the label class:<id>, counted by the gate, so a defect PR never edits this file (every PR appending here would hold every other by file overlap). A second closed row under one class:<id> is a REPEAT, and a repeat means the guard failed. `seed` lists the instances named when the file was written, with the BASIS for each: 'chairman-named' (the chairman's direction on #4122; class membership not re-read by ceo), 'title states it' (ceo read the row title, which says so), 'ceo read'. Re-read the row before relying on a seed. `guard` is a detector or rule IN FORCE that stops the class everywhere, or null with a guardNote saying what is missing or still unmerged: a control that is ordered, open or partial is a guardNote, never a guard. A class with a null guard is the first thing to fix. An instance with no row number (a pull request in another repository) is written <owner/name>#<n>. EVENT KINDS (#4450, epic #4437 move 1a): the entries from `main-red` on are EVENT kinds, not row defects. They have no `class:<id>` label and no closed rows: an instance is a line of the host's `failure-ledger` (`<kind>\t<ts ms>\t<ref>`), and a repeat is one kind with two or more distinct refs (`repeatsIn`).

classes.guardNote: none in force. Ordered 2026-10-08 on #4084 and unfiled when this was written: a shared-CI check that a PR touching a releasablePaths entry carries a changeset or a 'no-release: <reason>' line, and an org-health cause when main is ahead of the latest release for over a day. Set guard to that rule when both merge.

classes.name: A hold or a wait written in a form no gate reads (a prose umbrella, a Waiting-for line on a PR the gate does not scan), so it outlives its condition.
classes.guardNote: none that covers the class. Waiting conditions are fields (rules/waiting-conditions.md) and pr:hold --until clears them, but a keyed-repository PR hold is not read by pr:hold, so a resolved hold on an agent-org PR waits for its owner (agent-org#369, #374 on 2026-10-08). The 'gate lifts a resolved keyed-repository hold' row is unfiled; a control that leaves the case open is not a guard for the class.

classes.name: A row is parked with no condition that will ever un-park it, so it sits until a person notices.
classes.guardNote: none named. #4050 un-parks a row whose every condition came TRUE; it does not catch a parked row that has no condition at all.

classes.name: An epic whose children are done stays open, because no rule says who closes it or on what reading.
A detector reports to the managers something they cannot act on, or reports it repeatedly, so alarms cost a turn each and are read less.
classes.guardNote: none in force. #4065 (org-health: one wake per new signal class or severity crossing, suppression logged, the rest in a digest) is open; set guard to it when it merges.

classes.name: Two versions of one tool run at once (an installed copy beside a checkout, a pinned release beside main), so a fix is merged and not in effect.
classes.guardNote: none named. Related rows that mention it but are not seeded as instances: #3316, #3468.

classes.name: Scope is added to a row after it is claimed and folded into the claimed row instead of filed as its own, so the row grows past what its Acceptance named and cannot be finished.
classes.guardNote: none in force. The gate comparison (a claimed row whose scope grew after the claim, or a mirror whose scope exceeds its original) is the sibling a11ign/agent-org row and is not merged. Set guard to its reference when it merges. Until then the only control is the product-manager role file sentence: scope added to a claimed row is a new row.

classes.guardNote: none in force. Four controls are merged and each is partial. Row-file refuses an unsplit Done-when (agent-org#546, 2026-10-09T20:59:00Z) at FILING only, so a wait that arises after filing, or in a row filed before it, is not refused. The gate releases a claim that holds nothing and reaches a wait declared as Not-before, answer:<another session>, needs:chairman or Waiting-for: (agent-org#545, 2026-10-09T20:44:45Z), so a wait declared in none of the four, a holder with work in hand and an open pull request keep the claim, and the release does not file the remainder as its own row. The daily pass records a claim idle over 60 minutes with no open PR, or a PR with nothing pending, as a row-not-finishable ledger incident (agent-org#547, 2026-10-09T20:53:31Z): once a day with the retrospective, and it records only, releasing and closing nothing. A build row that closes on merge files its verify row (agent-org#556, 2026-10-09T21:26:33Z) for the future-time item only, so another seat's decision or another row's outcome gets none. Not built as of this entry: a rule that flags or closes a row left open after its deliverable's pull request merged (the chairman's 30-minute detector, #4437 comment 6095588368). Set guard to that rule's reference when it is in force.

classes.name: `main` is red: a trunk run of the code repository failed. Recorded per red RUN by the tick (`readTrunkRed`).
classes.guard: `readTrunkRed` in `src/trunk-red.ts` of a11ign/agent-org reads a declared code repository's newest `push` and `schedule` runs (`CODE_REPOSITORY_EVENT_FILTERS`, one call each, the newest of either deciding) and counts as red `main` a red push run, a red `cross-repo` leg whose `gate` read green (`continue-on-error` keeps the run and the required check green, so the leg's own job conclusion is read), and a red nightly. `trunkRedOrders` then wakes the fixer WITH the answer: the merging session of the newest commit with `product-manager` as its way out, and `product-manager` for a nightly, which has no commit of its own. Row a11ign/agent-org#539, merged as a11ign/agent-org#650 (2026-10-10T12:32:14Z). `src/trunk-red.test.ts` in agent-org pins it, each read with a negative control: the leg green, a repository with no such leg, a job that only contains the words, a refused runs read, and a green push or nightly that clears an older red. It stands in force since that merge; before it a red leg or nightly went unowned for 11 pushes.
classes.guardNote: recorder: the tick, from #4450 (`mainRedEvents` in `src/failure-ledger.ts` of agent-org). Not covered: the ref of a ledger event is the red RUN, so a standing red is counted once per run and a leg red for N pushes is N occurrences of one class, which is how this class's own repeat row #4833 was filed (lab runs 38045596539 and 38055200478 were one red `checks (cross-repo)` leg, not two); the near-duplicate is not collapsed by the recorder or by `repeatsIn`. A leg is found by the NAME `cross-repo` (`CROSS_REPO_LEG`), so a `continue-on-error` job of another name reads green, and only a repository declared as a code repository (`trunkOfCodeRepository`, read by `scopeTick`) is read at all. A stuck agent-org red is reported, not escalated to `answer:ceo` (`stuckRowOf` reads `pr-<n>` as a row of the primary). The reading is as of agent-org `origin/main` a6d68f5f, 2026-10-10.

classes.name: The owner ladder (`ownerOfPr`) named nobody for a pull request, so its order fell to the `ceo` rung.
classes.guard: Three rungs of `ownerOfPr` now name an owner where none was named: `isDependencyBotPr` (a11ign/agent-org#542) names the owner of a bot pull request; `owner-gone` (a11ign/agent-org#548, row #4644) names `product-manager` for a pull request whose owner session ended and every row it closes is closed; and, since a11ign/agent-org#637 (row #4808), the same rung also fires when the closing row is OPEN and held by nobody (`closingRowsUnheld`), the #4805 shape. `src/packaging/pr-owner-gone.test.ts` in agent-org pins both halves of the rung (the #4626 closed-row case and the #4805 open-and-unclaimed case, each with a CONTROL where the row is claimed or the label alive), and the grid oracle in `src/packaging/pr-owner-total.test.ts` pins that `ownerOfPr` names a session for every cell.
classes.guardNote: Not covered: a pull request with NO label whose branch names no row still falls to the `ceo` rung and is recorded by `unresolvedOwnerEvents` (recorder: the tick, from #4450). #4386 is the resolver defect it first showed. Also unfixed: the merge-conflict order's own `owner-gone` sentence (`src/work-gate/shared-file-orders.ts`) still says "the row it closed is closed", false for an open-unclaimed row (named by a11ign/agent-org#637 as a follow-up).

classes.name: A change a human-side session made that the org should have made itself (`hand-fix-ledger`).
classes.guard: `classifyLogin` in `src/hand-fix-ledger.ts` of a11ign/agent-org reads a dependency bot (`app/dependabot`, `dependabot[bot]`, Renovate, from the one `DEPENDENCY_BOT_LOGIN` definition) as `automation`, so its pull request is no longer counted as a human-side change: row a11ign/agent-org#560, built on #705, merged as a11ign/agent-org#716 (b7a247af, 2026-10-10T19:19:17Z). `src/packaging/hand-fix-ledger.test.ts` pins it, with controls that a human bump, a lookalike login (`dependabot-fan`) and a declared `Hand-fix:` are still counted. This stops the FALSE occurrences: 23 of this row's 30 ledger lines were Dependabot pull requests (read with `gh pr view` on each ref, row #4623 comment 6089529937).
classes.guardNote: recorder: the tick, from #4450, once a day, per counted change. NOT stopped: the 7 genuine occurrences (#2950, #2988, #3001, #2990, #3003, #3018, #3017, all merged 2026-10-02) were org-authored changes with a declared `Hand-fix:` line, each of which built the gate or detector its own line names; the recorder counts them correctly and nothing prevents a human-side session fixing a gap the org should have closed, only the gates those seven produced. None newer than 2026-10-02 is genuine in the ledger as read 2026-10-09. Whether that residual is itself a guard is `ceo`'s call. The ledger was not re-read after #716, so the post-fix count is not measured.

classes.guardNote: Not covered: `readProseAndOrder` is the only `answer:<session>` writer found (by reading every `answer:` string in `src/` of agent-org), so a writer added elsewhere, or a label added by hand or by a one-shot script, does not pass through the guard. The label names the comment's AUTHOR, not the handoff's target (noted on #4679, not repaired). The writer of the 2026-10-09 burst was never positively identified in the journal; it is inferred to be `readProseAndOrder` replaying past labels, so a repeat from another path would not be refused.

classes.name: A claimed worker stopped mid-task, or a stalled holder or a spare held the slot a ready row needed, and nothing woke it or started another.
classes.guard: Two merged controls in a11ign/agent-org: #597 (row #458) wakes a claimed worker that is `idle` or `done` with a claim naming a branch, no open pull request, no pending check and no declared wait field, with a "continue" order after 10 minutes (`STOPPED_CLAIMANT_MINUTES`), tells a holder whose agent-session id changed that its background tasks are lost, and appends one `claimed-worker-stalled` event to the failure ledger per nudge (`src/idle-claimant-stopped.test.ts`, `src/claim-stall-restart-notice.test.ts`); #599 (row #459) types a spare `worker-<n>` only the row it was named for (`ownRowOnly` in `wake.ts`), so an unclaimed ready row starts a FRESH worker rather than a second row being typed into a standing session (`src/ready-row-dispatch.test.ts`).
classes.guardNote: Not covered: the 10-minute figure is capped below the measured healthy-wait tail (p90 11.3, p95 16.5 minutes), so some healthy waits draw one unneeded "continue" (#597 counted 18 of 146 in three weeks); a holder that has an open pull request or a declared wait stays on the 45-minute idle and 120-minute no-progress clocks; the 10-minute rule was replayed on four workers of #4437, not read on a live tick when #597 merged. A tick-written ledger event is a nudge, not proof the worker resumed.

classes.name: The trace store goes stale while sessions are working, so nobody reads the org's own metrics and nobody is told.
classes.guard: One merged control in a11ign/agent-org: #498 gives the trace store a clock of its own, `a11ign-trace-ingest.timer` (`host/trace-ingest.timer.in`, every five minutes, `OnUnitActiveSec=5min`), which runs `src/trace/freshness.ts`. That file ingests (`trace -- --ingest`) and then asks whether the store is stale: no `turn` event for 10 minutes (`STALE_AFTER_MS`, the chairman's figure on a11ign#4437) while a transcript has changed in the last 10 minutes. A stale store raises ONE incident per episode, a comment on the standing row #928 and an order to the owning seat (`orchestrator`) under `Class: metrics-outage`, each effect retried next run if refused. Pinned in `src/trace/freshness.test.ts` (and the unit's wiring in `src/host-units.ts` / `src/packaging/host-units.test.ts`). The timer was listed active on this host on 2026-10-10.
classes.guardNote: Not covered: the check lives in the same unit it watches, so a timer that is disabled or a host that is down raises nothing; "working" is a transcript modified inside the window, so a single tool call longer than 10 minutes that is the only thing running can read as stale, and a healthy store reads about five minutes old; the incident is one comment and one order per episode, so nothing confirms the seat acted on it. Read from agent-org origin/main and the timer's listing, not from a live incident: no stale episode was observed raised end to end. The incident's ref is empty on the org-health line (a separate row against agent-org, not this one).
